research_question: Does a large absolute CFTC Legacy Non-Commercial Net/Open Interest imbalance predict short-horizon FX reversal over the next five trading days?

hypothesis.primary: When Net/OI is at or above +30%, subsequent local-currency-vs-USD return is expected to be negative; when Net/OI is at or below -30%, subsequent return is expected to be positive.
hypothesis.economic_interpretation: Very large absolute speculative imbalances may represent crowding and reduced marginal capacity to extend the same directional position.
hypothesis.independence_from_prior_tests: This experiment tests an absolute imbalance threshold that predates the current backtests in the project's canonical COT reporting rules. It is not tuned from the failed weekly-flow test or the passed 104-week percentile test.

signal.threshold_source: Canonical Weekly COT G8 reporting rule already in use before this experiment: |Net/OI| >= 30% is a material imbalance alert.

fx_return_definition.orientation: positive return always means local currency strengthens versus USD
fx_return_definition.entry: first available daily FX close on or after research_available_from
fx_return_definition.exit: fifth subsequent FX trading-day close after entry

chronology.split_rule: Within each currency, first 60 percent of eligible labeled imbalance-signal observations by entry date are diagnostic-only; final 40 percent are frozen OOS evaluation.
chronology.split_rounding: floor(0.60 * N) observations assigned to diagnostic segment
